lessonTitle: Power Transmission and Statically Indeterminate Shafts

blocks.text: A wind-turbine gearbox output shaft turns slowly but pushes tens of kilonewton metres into the generator, while the high-speed shaft carrying the same power is slender. The same power calls for very different shafts depending on speed, because power is torque times angular speed.

blocks.markdown: A rotating shaft transmits **power** $P = T\omega$, where $T$ is torque (N m) and $\omega$ the angular speed (rad/s). With a speed of $n$ revolutions per minute, $\omega = 2\pi n/60$. With $P$ in watts and $T$ in N m, power in kW is $P=T\omega/1000$. Once the torque is known, the diameter follows from the torsion formula and an allowable shear stress $\tau_{\text{allow}}$ (typically a fraction of yield stress, chosen with a safety factor).

blocks.title: From power to diameter
blocks.text: For a solid shaft, $\tau_{\max}=16T/(\pi d^3)$, so the minimum diameter is $d=\left(16T/(\pi\tau_{\text{allow}})\right)^{1/3}$. Doubling torque for the same stress increases the diameter by only $2^{1/3}=1.26$.

blocks.caption: $P$ in W, $T$ in N m, $n$ in rev/min; use $T$ in N mm with $\tau$ in MPa to get $d$ in mm.

blocks.title: Sizing a shaft for a motor
blocks.prompt: A shaft must transmit 75 kW at 1500 rev/min. The allowable shear stress is 50 MPa. Find the torque and the minimum solid diameter.
blocks.answer: T = 477.5 N m and the shaft diameter must be at least 36.5 mm (a standard size above this would be chosen, for example 38 mm).

blocks.markdown: **Statically indeterminate shafts.** If a shaft is fixed at both ends and a torque $T_0$ is applied at an intermediate section, the two reaction torques $T_A$ and $T_B$ cannot be found from $T_A+T_B=T_0$ alone. Compatibility requires the net rotation of one end relative to the other to be zero, so the twist of segment AC equals (in magnitude) the twist of segment CB: $T_A L_1/(G J_1)=T_B L_2/(G J_2)$.

blocks.title: Shaft fixed at both ends
blocks.prompt: A uniform shaft of length 1.0 m is fixed at both ends. A torque of 900 N m is applied at section C, 0.4 m from the left end A. Find the end reactions.

steps.text: Compatibility: A and B do not rotate, so twist in AC (due to T_A) equals twist in CB (due to T_B); GJ is constant.

blocks.answer: The reactions are 540 N m at A and 360 N m at B; the nearer, shorter and stiffer part takes more.

rows: Linear, material near axis is lightly stressed
Larger outer diameter, thin walls may buckle
blocks.caption: Solid versus hollow shafts

blocks.markdown: **Hollow versus solid.** Material near the axis carries little stress, so removing it costs little strength but saves much weight. For the same material and allowable stress, equal torque capacity requires equal $J/c$. Mass per unit length is proportional to the cross-sectional area.

blocks.title: Mass saving of a hollow shaft
blocks.prompt: A solid shaft of diameter 60 mm is to be replaced by a hollow shaft of outer diameter 75 mm with the same torque capacity and the same material. Find the inner diameter and the ratio of masses.

steps.text: Equal capacity means equal J/c. For the solid shaft J/c = pi d^3/16; compare (d_o^4 - d_i^4)/d_o = d^3.
Solve for the inner diameter with d_o^4 = 3.164e7.

blocks.answer: The hollow shaft has di = 62.7 mm and weighs only about 47 percent of the solid shaft, saving more than half of the mass.

blocks.title: Check thin walls
blocks.text: Highly hollow shafts save the most mass but have thin walls that may buckle or be unable to carry stress concentrations at keyways. Use SI-consistent units, and remember that rpm must be converted to rad/s before using P = T omega.

points: Power transmitted is P = T omega with omega = 2 pi n/60; the same power needs a bigger torque, and a bigger shaft, at lower speed.
A shaft fixed at both ends is indeterminate: equilibrium gives T_A + T_B = T_0 and compatibility sets the net twist across the whole shaft to zero.
A hollow shaft gives the same torque capacity as a solid one with much less mass because the central material is lightly stressed.

questions.stem: A shaft turns at 600 rev/min. What is its angular speed in rad/s?

distractorRationale.b: This is the number of revolutions per minute, not rad/s.
distractorRationale.d: This is rad per minute (2 pi x 600), not per second.

questions.explanation: Convert revolutions per minute to rad/s using omega = 2 pi n/60. For n = 600 this gives 62.8 rad/s, the value to use in P = T omega.

questions.stem: A solid shaft transmits a given power at speed n and is sized for a fixed allowable shear stress. If the speed is halved while the power is unchanged, by what factor must the diameter increase?

distractorRationale.c: Correct: T doubles, d scales as T^(1/3) = 1.26.
distractorRationale.d: Wrong direction: lower speed needs a larger shaft.

questions.explanation: For constant power, T = P/omega doubles when speed is halved. Since d is proportional to T^(1/3), the diameter grows by 2^(1/3) = 1.26.

questions.stem: A uniform shaft is fixed at both ends and a torque T_0 is applied at its mid-length. What is the reaction torque at each end?

distractorRationale.a: Correct: symmetry plus compatibility gives equal reactions.
distractorRationale.b: Would need one end carrying the entire torque.
distractorRationale.d: Reactions together equal T_0 and cannot exceed it.

questions.explanation: Equilibrium requires T_A + T_B = T_0. By symmetry (equal lengths, same GJ), the twist in each half is the same only if the reactions are equal, so each is T_0/2.

questions.stem: Why can a hollow shaft carry the same torque as a solid shaft with considerably less mass?

options.text: The shear stress in a hollow shaft is uniform across the wall
Hollow shafts have a larger shear modulus
The stress is zero in a hollow shaft
Material near the axis is lightly stressed, so removing it hardly reduces J/c

questions.correctOptionText: Material near the axis is lightly stressed, so removing it hardly reduces J/c

distractorRationale.a: The stress still varies with radius, though less across a thin wall.
distractorRationale.b: G is a material property, not shape.
distractorRationale.c: Stress is non-zero in the walls.
distractorRationale.d: Correct: stress is proportional to radius, so inner material contributes little to torque.

questions.explanation: Shear stress and the contribution to torque are proportional to r and r^2 respectively, so material close to the axis adds little to J. Moving material outwards raises J/c for a given mass.

questions.stem: True or false: for a fixed torque, the power transmitted by a shaft is proportional to its rotational speed.
questions.explanation: Since P = T omega, doubling speed at constant torque doubles the power. This is why high-speed shafts of the same power carry smaller torque.

questions.stem: A motor delivers 22 kW at 900 rev/min through a solid shaft. The allowable shear stress is 40 MPa. Find the minimum shaft diameter in mm.

A shaft is fixed at both ends. Segment AC (diameter 30 mm, length 0.5 m) and segment CB (diameter 20 mm, length 0.5 m) are made of the same material. A torque of 1000 N m is applied at C. Find the magnitude of the reaction torque at end B in N m.

A solid shaft is replaced by a hollow shaft of the same material with the same torque capacity, whose inner diameter is 0.8 times its outer diameter. Find the mass of the hollow shaft as a percentage of the solid shaft's mass.
questions.explanation: Equal capacity gives d_o^3(1 - 0.8^4) = d^3, so d_o = 1.193 d. Area ratio = 1.193^2 x (1 - 0.64) = 0.512, i.e. 51.2 percent.

questions.stem: Explain why, for the same power, a shaft running at low speed must be larger than one running at high speed. Include the relevant equations.
markingGuide: Deduces T = P/omega, so lower omega gives higher torque
Relates diameter to torque through tau_max = 16T/(pi d^3)
Concludes d is proportional to T^(1/3), so larger diameter at low speed
Mentions the need to convert rev/min to rad/s
questions.explanation: Because power is torque times speed, a slow shaft must carry more torque. The torsion formula then requires a larger diameter to keep the shear stress within the allowable value.

questions.stem: Describe how the reactions of a circular shaft fixed at both ends and loaded by a torque at an intermediate section are found, and why the problem is statically indeterminate.
markingGuide: Equilibrium gives one equation T_A + T_B = T_0 with two unknowns
Identifies the problem as statically indeterminate
Compatibility: net relative rotation between the fixed ends is zero
Writes twist in each segment as T L/(GJ) and equates them
Solves the pair of equations to give both reaction torques
questions.explanation: Statics alone only fixes the sum of the end torques. The geometric condition that the ends cannot rotate relative to each other provides the second equation.
